text:
**Screen summary: site at 0.498, 33.14, Uganda (hydro, 5 km radius)**

The site sits on the Victoria Nile at Bujagali Falls, and the gazetteer lists an existing hydropower station and substation on the footprint. Any hydro asset here would be an expansion, upgrade or rehabilitation in a populated, biodiverse river corridor, so all four Performance Standards screen in. This is a place screen only; I did not look for project documents.

**PS5 (land acquisition, livelihoods): high.** OSM maps 79 settlement features on the footprint, including villages named Buwenda, Budondo, Buloba, Buyala and Kabowa at 0 km. It also maps 20 farmland or meadow polygons on site and a residential area 0.58 km away. Dense occupation implies likely displacement and livelihood loss. Informal settlements are rarely mapped, so the true occupancy is probably higher.

**PS6 (biodiversity, natural resources): high.** The Victoria Nile runs through the footprint. Forest reserves lie 0.43 to 5.2 km away (Namavundu, Kimaka Range, Nsube, Kagoma), and forest or woodland features are on site. GBIF records within 5 km include Critically Endangered Haplochromis cichlids (several species, on site, 2009–2015), Critically Endangered Hooded Vulture (on site, 2025), and Endangered Grey Parrot and Grey Crowned-Crane (on site, 2025). A further 30 threatened species are recorded within 20 km. Fish records are likely to reflect river-flow dependence. The record set was truncated at 300 of 335 and is unevenly sampled.

**PS4 (community health and safety): high.** The footprint contains schools, a hospital and a health centre (about 80 community facilities on site, 297 within 5 km). Existing grid infrastructure (Bujagali and Kiira plants, substations) is nearby. Dam safety and traffic are relevant. Main roads are present, so new access is probably limited.

**PS7 (Indigenous Peoples): low, not triggered.** No Indigenous or community land is mapped within 20 km. OSM coverage is weak and customary tenure is not mapped, so this rests on the absence of data.

**PS8 (cultural heritage): medium, triggered.** Three places of worship are on site and another is 0.9 km away. Bujagali Falls is a named natural feature with a Wikipedia entry. No heritage site is mapped within 5 km, but chance-find risk for the falls and riverbank remains open.

**Category A.** The drivers are PS5 displacement, PS6 threatened aquatic and terrestrial species in the river corridor, and PS4 dam safety in a populated area.

**Context.** No international boundary lies within 20 km. I could not check Ugandan country risk (governance, security, sovereign rating) with these tools, so that needs a separate source. The Wikipedia link below is the only desk-research lead the gazetteer returned; the tool gave no publication dates.

**Key gaps:** the OSM data is incomplete, the GBIF data is sampling-biased, customary land tenure is unmapped, and there is no flow, hydrology, sediment or cultural-significance data. These need field or specialist review before any rating is final.

You are a geospatial analyst doing a desk-based screen of a project site for environmental and social (non-technical) risk, in IFC Performance Standard terms. You can only see the site's location, country and asset type. Use the tools to look at open data around the site.

Finish with a summary for a person of no more than 400 words, then exactly one JSON block in a ```json fence:
{
  "themes": [{"ps": "PS5", "rating": "high|medium|low|not_assessed", "triggered": true,
              "evidence": [{"concept": "", "name": "", "distance_km": 0, "source": ""}],
              "desk_research": [{"finding": "", "url": "", "date": ""}], "gaps": ""}],
  "ps5": true, "ps6": true, "ps7": false, "ps8": false,
  "category": "A|B|C",
  "category_drivers": [""],
  "context": {"country_risk": [], "social": []},

"ps5" to "ps8" mean: would IFC expect this Performance Standard to apply to the project?
Screen the place, not a particular project: don't try to work out which project this is or look up documents about it.

Use your own judgement about which data to check and how to interpret it.
